methodology: Codex independently reopened every model-cited URL, checked direct page content, redirects and current status, reopened the 2019 transaction sources and 2021 SEC filing, reviewed the current GRESB participant page and Argo responsible-investing page, and searched explicitly for a later Pearl/Ruby sale, transfer, restructuring, dissolution or signed pending exit.

verifiedClaims: Onyx announced the sale of its sponsor-equity interest in a 114 MW distributed-generation solar portfolio to funds managed by Argo.
The portfolio consisted of fully contracted operating assets with more than 20 years of weighted-average contracted life.
CohnReznick Capital described the transaction as a successfully executed structured-equity sale.
Funds managed by Argo invested in the 114 MW C&I solar portfolio by February 5, 2019.
The portfolio comprised 134 sites in 12 states that entered operations from 2015 through 2018.
Onyx constructed and financed the assets and was expected to continue managing them.
Ballard Spahr represented Argo-managed funds on the 114 MW portfolio investment.
The source corroborates 134 sites, 12 states and long-term PPAs.
The source describes completion of Argo's solar-platform establishment but does not provide a separate legal closing date.
A June 2021 Argo presentation filed with the SEC lists Pearl/Ruby Solar among Argo's holdings.
The filing identifies Pearl/Ruby as a 114 MW C&I solar portfolio with assets in 12 states.
The filing separately lists Astro Solar, confirming the two portfolios must not be merged.
The current GRESB participant page lists Pearl\ Ruby as a non-listed Americas renewable-power asset.
The asset is classified as photovoltaic solar generation.
The page separately lists Argo Infrastructure Partners LP as an infrastructure fund manager, but does not itself expose a direct asset-to-manager join.
Argo states that it participates in GRESB as a firm and through its portfolio companies.
Argo describes ongoing asset-management and stewardship across its managed investments in 2025.
This source supplies manager-level context but does not individually name Pearl/Ruby.
Argo said on July 9, 2026 that its existing U.S. C&I solar platform remained active and expanded to 196 sites and 270 MW.
The newly acquired NuGen sites are an aggregate-platform expansion and not separate evidence of Pearl/Ruby's legal title.
The source is retained only as current supporting context and not as sole Pearl/Ruby ownership evidence.

exitSearchConclusion: No later Pearl/Ruby-level sale, transfer, dissolution or signed pending transaction was identified through August 16, 2026. The 2021 SEC holding, current GRESB asset listing, Argo's current GRESB participation and its July 2026 description of an active expanded C&I solar platform collectively support retaining Argo as active, while the exact fund, vehicle, legal title and percentage remain not publicly disclosed.
